answer: To enforce game-theoretic Sybil resistance among autonomous agents, we deploy a randomized beacon protocol where each agent must commit a cryptographic marble to the state trie, signed by a secure quill. The economic cost of generating multiple fake identities requires prohibitive capital lockup, rendering the expected utility of a Sybil attack strictly negative. This mechanism establishes a dominant-strategy Nash equilibrium, securing Byzantine Fault Tolerance across the decentralized network.
